item.title: AI leaders warn UN of security risks as systems grow more powerful
item.description:
UNITED NATIONS, Sept 23 (Reuters) - The world's leading artificial intelligence companies warned the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday of the [risks](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/ten-days-that-changed-course-ai-2026-09-19/) ​posed by AI to humanity, appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful technology.
Governments around ​the world have struggled to keep pace with rapid advances in artificial intelligence.
## US TO UN: YOU CANNOT GOVERN TECHNOLOGY YOU DON'T UNDERSTAND UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who has ⁠long pushed ​for global governance of AI, has warned that rapidly advancing artificial intelligence poses risks that cannot be ignored, ​putting him at odds with Trump.

item.title: Trump says AI will be renamed ‘super intelligence’ in all US documents
Bernie Sanders and Greg Casar propose AI ‘superintelligence’ ban with a 20-year jail penalty
item.description:
Greg Casar, D-Texas, rolled out an aggressive bill Wednesday to rein in artificial intelligence, escalating the debate on Capitol Hill.
The 19-page [Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act](https://www.sanders.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/Ban-Artificial-Superintelligence-Act.pdf) would require pausing advanced AI development until a Cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence, led by a secretary of AI, can be created to regulate and supervise it.
The lines were further blurred by President Donald Trump’s announcement that he would rename “artificial intelligence” to “ [super intelligence](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/trump-address-united-nations-general-assembly-iran-war-rcna599085)” for the purposes of government documents in his speech Tuesday at the United Nations General Assembly.

item.title: Community colleges ask state for nearly $200 million to support AI adoption
item.description:
The California Community Colleges system is requesting nearly $200 million from the state to support the adoption of artificial intelligence across its 116 colleges.
As [higher education institutions nationwide](https://www.sacbee.com/news/local/education/article317271030.html) grapple with the entry of this new technology into their classrooms, boardrooms and systems, the California Community Colleges system has identified artificial intelligence as one of its major budget priorities for next year.
## Planned AI initiatives Another $25 million will be spent setting up the Artificial Intelligence Innovation Fund, which will provide competitive grants to individual districts to pilot projects that may improve teaching and learning, and $9 million on incorporating agentic AI into the system’s statewide technology ecosystem.
